references.text: Joseph explains that dream interpretation belongs to God and offers to interpret the dreams of Pharaoh's servants. This demonstrates his ability to interpret dreams, which Pharaoh has now heard about.
The cupbearer tells Pharaoh about Joseph and his ability to interpret dreams in prison. This is the direct reason why Pharaoh turns to Joseph in verse 15.
Joseph answers Pharaoh that it is not he who can give an answer, but that God will give Pharaoh a favorable response. This emphasizes that dream interpretation comes from God.
Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dreams and explains their meaning, in response to Pharaoh's request in verse 15.
Daniel explains to King Nebuchadnezzar that no wise men can interpret the dream, but that there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets. The parallel with Joseph before Pharaoh is striking.
The verses illuminate each other by showing how God's revelation leads to human recognition of divine wisdom.
It illuminates the theological mechanism behind Joseph's ability to interpret dreams by defining God's way of revealing Himself.
